sources.title: François Bruhat, Lectures on Lie Groups and Representations of Locally Compact Groups (TIFR Lectures 14)
sources.locator: Part III, Chapter 10, §§1.1–1.8, printed pp.90–102 (PDF pp.100–110)
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 140-page PDF and inspected the whole relevant Chapter 10 argument on printed pp.90–102: fundamental families, section criterion, the Hilbert completion, measurable operator fields, norm equality, the commutant proof, and weak closure of diagonal multipliers. Bruhat's topological/Lusin field convention is not silently identified with the modern measurable-field convention used in this scaffold.

contents.name: Countable fundamental families and measurable sections
contents.support: The authored proof explicitly codes every finite rational-complex combination, proves its density using rational density in R, and uses countable testing vectors to recover fibre norms and inner products without importing the Lusin-continuity equivalence.

contents.name: Direct-integral completion and fibrewise orthogonalization
contents.support: The proof derives the summable-subsequence completion, finite-measure pi-lambda approximation for scalar L², measurable fibrewise Gram–Schmidt, and Parseval coordinate density locally; AC selects the countable representative sequence and supplies the stated countable-choice hypotheses.

contents.name: Measurable operator fields and decomposable action
contents.support: The local proof derives measurability of the pointwise action from all-section coefficient testing, proves quotient well-definedness and the upper bound, constructs a countable normalized rational test family for the exact essential-supremum norm, and verifies fibre adjoint and product fields and their induced identities.

contents.name: Commutant of scalar diagonal multiplication
contents.support: Localize fundamental fields, glue representatives across an exhaustion, and use pointwise inequalities on a countable rational span.

contents.name: Theorem 3: weak closure of scalar multipliers
contents.support: The local proof makes the normalized fundamental sections and rank-one fields measurable, uses field uniqueness to obtain fibrewise commutation outside one countable-union null set, proves scalarity by diagonal and off-diagonal rank-one maps, and recovers a measurable bounded scalar on the least-index nonzero-fibre partition. Zero fibres and the nonfaithful multiplier kernel are explicit.

contents.name: Section 1.1 circle and real-line Fourier representation examples
contents.reason: These decompose particular group representations by Fourier transform; the assigned FA pair owns generic field and operator constructions, while Fourier and RG pages own these applications.

contents.name: Section 1.1 constant-fibre and counting-measure model
contents.support: The constant-fibre construction and discrete measure are specialized in the B example.

contents.name: Proposition 1 and continuous-section definition
contents.reason: The proposition characterizes continuity in Bruhat's locally compact topological field; this pair states a distinct countable measurable-section criterion over a standard-Borel base.

contents.name: Proposition 2: compact-uniform approximation of continuous sections
contents.reason: Its partition-of-unity and compact-uniform topology are specific to continuous fields; the present measurable direct integral uses rational fundamental sections and scalar L² density instead.

contents.name: Proposition 3: scalar-coefficient criterion for measurable vector fields
contents.support: The authored proof proves the countable coefficient test and measurable inner products directly, with explicit finite-sequence coding, rational coefficient density, and Borel measurability checks rather than importing Bruhat's Lusin definition.

contents.name: Proposition 4: measurable square-integrable sections characterize L²
contents.support: The quotient definition uses precisely measurable sections with finite integrated squared norm; completeness is proved in the next theorem.

contents.name: Section 1.5 fibrewise Gram–Schmidt construction
contents.support: The theorem constructs measurable fibrewise Gram–Schmidt sections, assigns zero to zero remainders, proves dense span, and uses the frame in a countable dense-set argument.

contents.name: Proposition 5: strongly continuous operator fields
contents.reason: This is a criterion for local topological continuity of operator fields; the assigned page only claims coefficient measurability and essential boundedness.

contents.name: Theorem 1: continuous finite-rank operator-field extension
contents.reason: The theorem extends continuous prescribed vectors over a compact subset; the modern measurable-field page uses directly defined rank-one fields and makes no extension claim.

contents.name: Proposition 6: matrix-coefficient measurability of operator fields
contents.support: The item proves locally that countable fundamental matrix coefficients are equivalent to testing all measurable sections, constructs a normalized countable rational test family, and proves operator-norm measurability by a countable pairing supremum. Bruhat’s local-boundedness and Lusin-continuity convention is recorded as different from the standard-Borel convention used here.

sources.title: Bachir Bekka and Pierre de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 445-page author monograph and inspected Chapter 1 §§1.G–1.H, printed pp.59–68, including the definitions, constant-field proof of Theorem 1.H.4, and the general-field theorem statement; pp.69–70 were inspected to delimit the separate von Neumann-algebra-field scope. The source refers its general-field proof to Dixmier, so the local scaffold gives the general-field reconstruction explicitly.

contents.name: Measurable fields and direct integrals
contents.support: Modern countable fundamental-family and section criterion with separable fibres.

contents.name: Square-integrable sections and the direct-integral inner product
contents.support: The definition follows the source's square-integrability quotient and fibre-integral pairing; it proves the quotient and inner-product properties locally and defers completeness to the next theorem.

contents.name: Constant-field and counting-measure models
contents.support: Constant separable fibre realizes vector-valued L² and counting measure realizes a Hilbert sum.

contents.name: Decomposable fields and diagonal commutant
contents.support: The source proves constant fibres via countable rational combinations and states the general-fibre theorem; the scaffold supplies the reduction-free general proof.

contents.name: Representation fields, irreducible decomposition, and factor criteria
contents.reason: The assigned FA page stops at generic direct-integral operator machinery; RG-24 and RG-26 are the planned destinations for representation-specific results.

contents.name: Proposition 1.G.2: dimension strata and constant-fibre models
contents.support: The spectral model uses measurable Gram–Schmidt and active-set rank enumeration to trivialize the fibre dimensions needed here; the source states the more general proposition and refers its proof elsewhere.

contents.name: Definitions 1.G.3–1.G.4: decomposable and diagonal operators
contents.support: The definition records Bekka–de la Harpe’s all-section measurability and essentially bounded action convention, while the local proof derives the countable coefficient criterion and measurable fibre norm. The source’s norm equality cites Dixmier–von Neumann and is not imported as proof.

contents.name: Proposition 1.G.5, Theorems 1.G.6, 1.G.8 and 1.G.10, Proposition 1.G.7, Examples 1.G.9 and 1.G.11
contents.reason: These named results concern induction, irreducible or factor representation fields, Plancherel applications, and non-type-I disintegration; the planned RG-24 and RG-26 pages own group-specific results.

contents.name: Theorem 1.H.1: general-field diagonal commutant
contents.support: The source states the general result but proves the constant-field case below; the scaffold reconstructs varying fields directly with localized fundamental sections.

contents.name: Proposition 1.H.2: WOT closure of constant-field diagonal multipliers
contents.support: The local proof extends the constant-field WOT-closure result to varying measurable fibres by showing D''=D through decomposable commutant fields, countably many measurable rank-one maps, almost-everywhere field uniqueness, and explicit zero-fibre scalar recovery; it does not assume the multiplier representation is faithful.

contents.name: Lemma 1.H.3: tensor-section totality
contents.support: The local proof uses localized normalized fundamental sections and scalar simple-function density in place of constant-field tensor totality.

contents.name: Theorem 1.H.4: constant-field commutant reconstruction
contents.support: The countable rational-span inequality is adapted to varying fibres with finite-measure localization and gluing.

contents.name: Corollary 1.H.5: multiplicity and maximal abelian diagonal algebra
contents.support: The B example proves the safe two-dimensional instance by explicit noncommuting matrix units; it does not assert the source's statement for a zero-dimensional constant fibre.

contents.name: Definitions 1.I.1 and 1.I.4, Examples 1.I.2 and 1.I.5, Proposition 1.I.3, Theorems 1.I.6–1.I.7
contents.reason: These concern measurable fields of von Neumann subalgebras and their decomposable-algebra commutants, beyond the scalar diagonal algebra of the assigned FA pair; planned RG-26 owns factor-field applications.

sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 338-page author-hosted PDF and read Proposition 3.1.3 with its countable projection-generator argument and Theorem 8.1.1 with the cyclic-module multiplicity construction and uniqueness argument. The local strategy makes the projection coding and diagonal closure explicit.

contents.name: Single self-adjoint generator of a separably acting abelian von Neumann algebra
contents.support: Take a countable WOT-dense family, countable spectral projections, and encode the commuting projections in one self-adjoint operator.

contents.name: Measurable multiplicity model
contents.support: Countable cyclic summands give a measurable multiplicity function with model fibres of dimensions in N union infinity.

contents.name: Proposition 3.1.2: cyclic vector for the commutant
contents.reason: The generator lemma uses WOT separability and countable spectral projections directly, and does not require a cyclic vector for the commutant.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1.4: maximal abelian cyclic model
contents.reason: This theorem assumes maximal abelianness and a cyclic scalar model; the assigned spectral theorem covers arbitrary separably acting abelian algebras with measurable multiplicity.

contents.name: Remark 8.1.2: self-adjoint spectral multiplicity interpretation
contents.support: The local theorem fixes a self-adjoint generator and its spectral coordinate before asserting measure-class and fibre-dimension uniqueness.

contents.name: Two-dimensional measurable operator field
contents.support: Specialize the measurable matrix-field criterion to an explicit 2-by-2 field and compute its norm and adjoint.

contents.name: Constant multiplicity two in an abelian diagonal representation
contents.support: The standard multiplicity field has two-dimensional fibres, while off-diagonal matrix units lie in the diagonal algebra's commutant.
